title: Pointwise exceptional Gysin comparison and its compositions
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and let $f:T\to S$ be a separated finite-type compactifiable morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use ordinary small-etale $D^+$ and the right adjoint $f^!$ to $Rf_!$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Put $C_sM=R\Gamma_sM$, using extraordinary restriction after localization as in [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. For $t\in T$, put $s=f(t)$, $a_t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, and $r_t=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-transcendence-degree]. For every $M\in D^+(S_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$\beta_{f,t,M}:a_t^*C_sM(r_t)[2r_t]\xrightarrow{\sim}C_t(f^!M).$$
Twists are the roots-of-unity twists of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. Its normalization is the Gysin normalization: on the fibre over $s$, take a regular nonempty open $U$ of the reduced closure of $t$; for $\pi:U\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, restrict the map $\pi^*C_sM(r_t)[2r_t]\to\pi^!C_sM$ to the generic point $t$. That map is obtained by factoring the regular scheme $U$ into a regular closed immersion in a smooth scheme over $\kappa(s)$, taking the regular-immersion fundamental class and the smooth purity map, and composing their exceptional comparisons. The regular-immersion class is the product of the codimension-one Kummer classes for a local regular sequence. The smooth map uses the diagonal-class/deformation and Kummer-normalized integration convention of [lem-trf-ambient-diagonal-purity-base-change]. The resulting $\beta$ is independent of these local factorizations and regular opens, and restricts to open subsets of source and target.

Under the right-adjoint transitivity isomorphism for composable $T\xrightarrow fS\xrightarrow gB$, the composite of $\beta_{g,s,M}$ and $\beta_{f,t,g^!M}$ is $\beta_{gf,t,M}$, with residue pullbacks and twist-shifts combined and $r_{gf,t}=r_{f,t}+r_{g,s}$. For a closed immersion $f$ it is the canonical supported-composition identification $C_t(f^!M)=C_{f(t)}M$, with $a_t$ the identity and $r_t=0$.

For a smooth $f$ of pure relative dimension $d$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the isomorphism $f^*M(d)[2d]\to f^!M$ of [lem-trf-ambient-diagonal-purity-base-change] has the following compatibility. If the $C_sM$ have pinnings, its induced costalk pinnings from $\beta$ are the fibrewise absolute-purity pinnings on $f^*M$, tensored by $(d)[2d]$, described in [lem-per-regular-pullback-pinnings]. Their degree is $\delta_S(s)+d-\dim\mathcal O_{T_s,t}=\delta_S(s)+r_t$. This is a comparison of the specified maps, including finite purely inseparable residue extensions, not only an existence of unnormalized isomorphisms.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.4.1 and the two following paragraphs; Proposition 2.4.3.1, Remark 2.4.3.2, Lemma 2.4.3.4; XVI, Theorems 2.5.5, 2.5.12 and 3.1.1 and Corollary 3.1.2; agent-formulated general-input version of the pointwise calculation, with smooth normalization specified by the current blueprint diagonal/deformation route

proof.text:
Fix $t$, put $s=f(t)$, $k=\kappa(s)$, $L=\kappa(t)$, and $N=C_sM$. Localize $S$ at $s$ and write $F=T\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\pi:F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The localization, fibre, and supported-composition comparisons of [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus] give
$$C_t(f^!M)\cong C_t(\pi^!N)\cong a_t^!N.$$
The second equality is computed by extraordinary restriction to the reduced closure of $t$ in $F$ and then restriction to its generic point. These are natural maps for every bounded-below $M$; no pinning or dualizing property has been used.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.4.1, first two sentences and fibrewise reduction

proof.text: Choose a nonempty regular affine open $U$ of the reduced closure of $t$ in $F$. To justify the choice, $k$ is excellent by [lem-exc-fields-excellent], so affine coordinate rings of this closure are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. Their regular loci are open by the J-2 clause of [def-exc-excellent-ring] and contain their generic point, whose local ring is a field and is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring]. Write $u:U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The regular-scheme Gysin theorem [lem-per-prime-power-regular-gysin] gives a factorization-independent isomorphism $\operatorname{Cl}_u:\Lambda_U(r_t)[2r_t]\to u^!\Lambda_k$; its virtual dimension is $r_t$ by that theorem's field-base clause. In particular this argument does not replace regularity by smoothness over a possibly imperfect field.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.4.1, regular-open choice; XVI, Corollary 3.1.2

proof.text:
Extend the constant class to the actual input $N$ by the specified tensor map:
$$\operatorname{Cl}_u(N):u^*N(r_t)[2r_t]\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Cl}_u\otimes1}u^!\Lambda_k\otimes^Lu^*N\xrightarrow{T_u(\Lambda,N)}u^!N.$$
The second arrow is invertible by [lem-per-field-exceptional-tensor], even for nonconstructible $N$ of infinite Tor amplitude. The first is invertible by [lem-per-prime-power-regular-gysin]. Restrict to $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and then use the inverse of the supported comparison from Step 1. This constructs $\beta_{f,t,M}$. It has the claimed direction, twist and shift, and is natural in $M$. Its defining map on $U$ is exactly regular-immersion Kummer class followed by the diagonal/deformation smooth comparison, with the same tensor transpose; it is therefore the required normalized map.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.4.1, displayed Gysin comparison, with its arbitrary-input tensor extension

proof.text: Two regular opens of the reduced closure have a common nonempty open containing its generic point. The classes on this intersection agree by the open-restriction clause of [lem-per-prime-power-regular-gysin], including independence of the regular closed/smooth factorization and of the defining sequence. Their coefficient extensions agree by restriction and naturality of $T$ in [lem-per-field-exceptional-tensor]. The supported comparisons agree by [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus]. Thus the maps at $t$ agree. Source and target open restrictions give the same construction because they preserve the residue fields, restrict the chosen regular opens, and commute with each of these three specified comparisons.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.4.1, independence of the regular open; XVI, Theorem 2.5.5

proof.text: For $T\xrightarrow fS\xrightarrow gB$, fix $t$, $s=f(t)$, $b=g(s)$ and use the field tower $\kappa(b)\subset\kappa(s)\subset\kappa(t)$. By the compositional supported comparisons of [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus], both proposed maps have target $a_t^!a_s^!C_bM$ with the right-adjoint transitivity normalization. By [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower], their source twists and shifts add to $(r_{gf,t})[2r_{gf,t}]$. On the essentially finite-type regular field maps, [lem-per-prime-power-regular-gysin] identifies the direct constant class with $a_t^!(\operatorname{Cl}_{a_s})\circ\operatorname{Cl}_{a_t}(r_{g,s})[2r_{g,s}]$. Expand each coefficient class as $T(\Lambda,-)\circ(\operatorname{Cl}\otimes1)$ as in Step 3. Naturality of $T$ moves $\operatorname{Cl}_{a_s}$ across the inner $T$, and the identity $T_{kh}=h^!T_k\circ T_h$ of [lem-per-field-exceptional-tensor] replaces the resulting two $T$ maps by $T_{a_sa_t}$. The result is exactly the direct coefficient class. Hence the two $\beta$ maps compose to $\beta_{gf,t,M}$.

source.place: XVII, paragraph following Lemma 4.4.1; XVI, Theorem 2.5.12

proof.text: If $f$ is closed, the residue extension is the identity and $r_t=0$. After the fibre reduction, the reduced closure of $t$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ itself. Its structure map, its constant Gysin class, and its coefficient tensor map are identities. Consequently the construction of Step 3 is precisely the inverse of $C_t(f^!M)\cong C_{f(t)}M$ from [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus], as required. For a finite purely inseparable field extension in characteristic $p\ne\ell$, [lem-per-prime-power-regular-gysin] instead gives multiplication by $[L:k]$; by tensoring, $\beta$ acts by that same unit on arbitrary $N$. This records the scalar rather than identifying the Gysin map with the identity of the equivalent etale topoi.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 2.4.3.1 and Proposition 2.4.3.3 proof; Lemma 4.4.1, following paragraph

proof.text: For the smooth clause put $F=T_s$, $k=\kappa(s)$ and $c=\dim\mathcal O_{F,t}$. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], $F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth of pure dimension $d$. Affine-locally its coordinate ring is a smooth $k$-algebra by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local] makes its local rings regular. In $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{F,t}$ the closed point immersion $i:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{F,t}$ is regular of codimension $c$: a regular system of parameters generates the maximal ideal by [def-weil-regular-scheme], and is a regular sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. Thus the localized fibre and this immersion satisfy the regular Gysin theorem's hypotheses, without a perfectness hypothesis on $k$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.1.1, regular fibre; regular closed point in the localized fibre

proof.text:
Suppose $p_s:N=C_sM\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(\delta_S(s))[2\delta_S(s)]$ is a given pinning. By [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus], regular supported base change identifies the fibre restriction of $f^*M$ with the pullback of $N$. Let
$$\rho_t:\Lambda(\delta_S(s)+d-c)[2\delta_S(s)+2d-2c]\longrightarrow C_t(f^*M(d)[2d])$$
be the map formed from $p_s^{-1}$ and the absolute-purity class of $i$ in Step 7, then twisted by $(d)[2d]$. This is the inverse pinning in the fibrewise recipe specified in [lem-per-regular-pullback-pinnings]. The smooth orientation of [lem-trf-ambient-diagonal-purity-base-change] restricts to the same orientation on $F/k$. By [lem-per-prime-power-regular-gysin], the constant class of the composite of $i$ with the localized smooth map to $k$ equals $i^!\operatorname{Cl}_{F/k}\circ\operatorname{Cl}_i(d)[2d]$. Extend this identity to $N$ using naturality and the tensor composition identity of [lem-per-field-exceptional-tensor]. The supported and smooth comparisons are the compatible ones specified in [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus], so the resulting equality of maps is
$$C_t(\gamma_f(M))\circ\rho_t=\beta_{f,t,M}\circ a_t^*(p_s^{-1})(r_t)[2r_t],$$
with the degree identification of Step 9. Taking inverses proves equality of the actual induced pinnings. This uses only the displayed fibrewise recipe, not the potentiality conclusion of the regular-pullback theorem for an arbitrary $M$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.1.1, regular fibre; regular closed point in the localized fibre

proof.text: The preceding fibre pinning on $f^*M$ has degree $\delta_S(s)-c$; after tensoring by $(d)[2d]$ it has degree $\delta_S(s)+d-c$. The dimension formula [lem-kun-dimension-formula] applied to the smooth pure $d$-dimensional $k$-scheme $F$ gives $d=c+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(t)$. Hence the degree is $\delta_S(s)+r_t$, with twist and cohomological shift twice the same integer. This also covers closed points ($c=d$) and generic fibre points ($c=0$).

from.place: Proof, Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality in the lower perverse bound; finite prime-power normalization underlying the regular generic duality model. Pointwise exceptional Gysin comparison and its compositions.

split_report.summary: Preserved the statement, constructed beta through the reduced fibre closure and canonical exceptional tensor map, and expanded choice independence, composition, closed-immersion and smooth-pinning comparisons. Added three statement-only prime-power tools: supported/essentially-finite-type restriction, regular-scheme Gysin classes, and field-base arbitrary-input exceptional tensor comparison. Existing F_ell tools do not cover ell^n; no compiler or Lean writing.
split_report.blueprint: Proof, Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality in the lower perverse bound; finite prime-power normalization underlying the regular generic duality model. Pointwise exceptional Gysin comparison and its compositions. Steps 1–9 implement the dimension-normalized generic-duality input, without changing the perverse-unit route.

tool_uses.why: Excellence of the arbitrary residue field ensures the chosen integral fibre closure has an open regular locus.
Excellence of finite-type fibre models and their localizations, used only for the regular-open construction.
The prescribed ordinary-etale smooth orientation with arbitrary inputs and its base-change equality, required for the smooth-pinning normalization.
The fibre local-dimension plus residue-transcendence-degree equality supplies the pinning degree.
Smoothness and the pure relative dimension persist on the residue fibre in the pinning comparison.
Regularity of the smooth fibre over its arbitrary, possibly imperfect residue field.
The parameters of the localized regular fibre give a regular immersion of its closed point, so absolute purity applies.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q19-204ef1332 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its 9 steps and the 3 new nodes in full, every cited node's statement, and ILO XVII 2.4.3.1–2.4.3.4, Cor 4.2.3, Lemmas 4.3.1.1, 4.3.1.2 and 4.4.1 with the paragraph after it. The statement is unchanged from base. Every step is supported by what the cited statements say: fibre and model restriction, the regular open of the reduced closure via J-2, beta as T_u∘(Cl_u⊗1), independence of choices, composition via the trdeg tower and T_{kh}=h^!T_k∘T_h, identity for closed immersions and [L:K] for inseparable extensions, the smooth pinnings through the lem-trf base-change equation and the regular-pullback recipe, and the degree d−c=r_t from 02FX. Small cases (identity, closed and generic points of A^1, inseparable extensions, non-flat N) all check out.
